source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
evidence_scope: Factual structured summary of printed species treatment and diagnostic key, not independently verified
cautions: Historical name concepts need separate modern taxonomic corroboration before scoring
Regional habitat and range statements do not establish Hays County nativity
Flora treats variety texensis; existing repository synonym crosswalk maps it to current subspecies texensis
Flower and fruit dimensions belong to C. canadensis species-level treatment and may overlap other subspecies

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Small thornless deciduous tree, frequently multi-trunked
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Leaf blades thick, leathery, cordate to cordate-reniform, wider than long; shiny, deep green and distinctly glaucous above
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Purple-red, rarely white; clusters of 2–6; petals ca. 9–12 mm long (species-level)
morphology_source_reported.fruits: Flat, slightly stipitate, 4–10 cm long × 8–18 mm wide (species-level)
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: Contrasts with var. canadensis in thick glossy wider-than-long rounded foliage versus thinner dull leaves
